5: ## IOMMU configuration {#iommu_config}
6: 
7: An IOMMU may be present and enabled on many platforms. When an IOMMU is present and enabled, it is
8: recommended that SPDK applications are deployed with the `vfio-pci` kernel driver. SPDK's
9: `scripts/setup.sh` script will automatically select `vfio-pci` in this case.
10: 
11: However, some devices do not function correctly when bound to `vfio-pci` and instead must be
12: attached to the `uio_pci_generic` kernel driver. In that case, users should take care to disable
13: the IOMMU or to set it into passthrough mode prior to running `scripts/setup.sh`.
14: 
15: To disable the IOMMU or place it into passthrough mode, add `intel_iommu=off`
16: or `amd_iommu=off` or `intel_iommu=on iommu=pt` to the GRUB command line on
17: x86_64 system, or add `iommu.passthrough=1` on arm64 systems.

52: Please note that the VFIO device isolation is based around IOMMU groups and it's
53: only possible to change permissions of the entire group, which might possibly
54: consist of more than one device. (You could also apply a custom kernel patch to
55: further isolate those devices in the kernel, but it comes with potential risks
56: as described on
57: [Alex Williamson's VFIO blog](https://vfio.blogspot.com/2014/08/iommu-groups-inside-and-out.html),
58: with the patch in question available here:
59: [[PATCH] pci: Enable overrides for missing ACS capabilities](https://lkml.org/lkml/2013/5/30/513))
60: 
61: Let's assume we want to use PCI device `0000:04:00.0`. First of all, verify
62: that it has an IOMMU group assigned:
63: 
64: ~~~{.sh}
65: readlink "/sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:00:04.0/iommu_group"
66: ~~~
67: 
68: The output should be e.g.
69: `../../../kernel/iommu_groups/5`
70: 
71: Which means that the device is a part of the IOMMU group 5. We can check if
72: there are any other devices in that group.
73: 
74: ~~~{.sh}
75: $ ls /sys/kernel/iommu_groups/5/devices/
76: 0000:00:04.0  0000:00:04.1  0000:00:04.2  0000:00:04.3  0000:00:04.4  0000:00:04.5  0000:00:04.6  0000:00:04.7
77: ~~~
78: 
79: In this case `0000:04:00.0` is an I/OAT channel which comes with 7 different
80: channels associated with the same IOMMU group.

89: ### Memory constraints {#system_configuration_nonroot_memory_constraints}
90: 
91: As soon as the first device is attached to SPDK, all of SPDK memory will be
92: mapped to the IOMMU through the VFIO APIs. VFIO will try to mlock that memory and
93: will likely exceed user ulimit on locked memory. Besides having various
94: SPDK errors and failures, this would also pollute the syslog with the following
95: entries:
96: 
97: `vfio_pin_pages: RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`
98: 
99: The limit can be checked by running the following command as target user:
100: (output in kilobytes)
101: 
102: ~~~{.sh}
103: ulimit -l
104: ~~~

findings: SPDK completion callback counts NVMe command completion/latency and replenishes unless draining; final loop drains outstanding command completions. This cannot be equated to iDMA byte completion.
iperf sender/receiver differ; bytes/blockcount termination options provide finite useful-work choices. Co-start with perf is an explicit experimental choice, not a sourced joint service demand.

SPDK VFIO group is an isolation/permission granularity; listed multi-channel example is I/OAT, not proof a selected NIC and SSD share a translation cache/PTW. UIO configuration may require bypass/off, so translation cannot be assumed.
yavta negotiated stride/sizeimage and actual bytesused, sequence/timestamps must be used. Nominal YUYV resolution cannot alone freeze DMA byte count.
skip7 suppresses save only; a successful c10 still dequeues10, allows last3 saves; lastnbufs iterations need not requeue. Do not substitute savedframes for capturedframes.
Specific default2025.1 dtsi disables SMMU and comments GEM mappings; not matched to historical SDI demo runtimeimage/overlay. No universal bypass claim.
Official SDI source proves memory capture topology, not IOMMU traversal or independent background workload.

For selected PCIe NVMe path, fn_table submits spdk_nvme_ns_cmd_read/write with io_complete; it reaches task_complete even on error. io_completed cannot be directly reported as successful useful bytes.
perf captures elapsed time before drain; source statistics require separate successful completion timestamps for exact fixed-window useful progress.
random storage LBA is not new host IOVA: normal task completion resubmits the same task/buffer, so preparation and stable-pool baselines remain applicable.
source_fact_vs_setting_limits: A pair of independent real benchmarks can be deliberately co-run, but this is not itself a natural workload contract.
No requirement that every experimental numeric choice be published or every task have a deadline.
A conditional ordinary-strategy failure hypothesis is not evidence of an observed failure.
Selected real hardware mappings and external service dependencies must be supplied or faithfully bounded before an executable model register.
architecture_clarification: Capture DDR ring does not have to fit private R2 96KiB SPM. Nominal12.44MiB ring alone is not a rejection reason; selected actual DDR/PTE footprint, producer stream/ownership/consumer cost and source timing still need acceptance.
